desc: OUSD(I) — since 2020 OUSD(I&S) — is the Office of the Secretary of Defense element responsible for intelligence, counterintelligence, security and sensitive activities policy across the Department, and it is the office in which the entire Elizondo dispute takes place. Elizondo worked there from 2008 until 4 October 2017, latterly as Director, National Programs Special Management Staff. Neill Tipton was its Director for Defense Intelligence (Collection & Special Programs); Garry Reid was its Director for Defense Intelligence (Intelligence & Security). It is the office that generated the December 2017 memoranda to the Secretary of Defense characterising Elizondo as having 'aggrandized his role', the office that in May 2019 coordinated the 'no assigned responsibilities' messaging line, and the office whose front office initiated the AFOSI inquiry into whether Elizondo had mishandled classified material. It is also, on Elizondo's account and on the face of his own DD Form 1910, the office from which the AATIP-associated video files were processed for clearance in August 2017 — five years after the Department says the program ended.

Under 50 U.S.C. 3373(b)(3)(B)(i), enacted by Section 6802(a) of the FY2023 NDAA, the Director of the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office reports to the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security on all administrative matters of the Office.

claims.text: Garry Reid, then Director for Defense Intelligence at OUSD(I), wrote a memorandum for record in late December 2017 asserting that Luis Elizondo had 'aggrandized his role' in AATIP and that to the best of Reid's knowledge Elizondo 'had no job responsibilities related to the AATIP.'

On 15 December 2017, the OUSD(I) Security Officer was notified that Elizondo may have 'misused government systems' and 'may intend to release [U.S. government] footage or information that he obtained during his employment with OUSD(I)' — a determination that presupposes he possessed such material.

On 18 December 2017 OUSD(I) discovered a classified email sent by Elizondo in August 2017 to a Navy civilian requesting assistance to get one or more videos declassified, with the same videos then circulating in the media attached; on 21 December 2017 Reid met AFOSI agents to initiate a formal inquiry into Elizondo's possible mishandling of classified materials.

A copy of Reid's memorandum for record bears handwritten marginal notes and initials dated '12/23' believed to be those of Secretary of Defense James N. Mattis, including a question whether Elizondo's 'sudden departure' constituted a 'counter-intelligence alarm?'

DoD reached its internal determination about Elizondo's AATIP role in late December 2017 but did not make it public until June 2019, an eighteen-month interval for which no reason appears in the released records.

Pentagon spokesperson Christopher Sherwood stated publicly in June 2019 that Elizondo 'had no responsibilities with regard to the AATIP program while he worked in OUSDI... up until the time he resigned effective 10/4/2017'; the department later revised the formulation to 'no assigned responsibilities.'

A previously unpublished Elizondo resignation letter received by his direct supervisor John Garrity III on 3 October 2017 surfaced in the FOIA release; the second, publicly known resignation letter was characterized in Reid's memo as having 'uncertain provenance' and as never delivered to the Secretary of Defense.

Reid's first security concern predates the New York Times story: on 12 October 2017 he learned of the To The Stars Academy launch at which Elizondo, one week after resigning, announced plans to provide 'never-before-released footage from real U.S. government systems,' and Reid contacted AFOSI, which found no 'tangible indicators' of misconduct at that time.

Garry Reid was removed from his position as Director for Defense Intelligence in April 2022 following a nearly two-year investigation by The Debrief; the stated cause was an inappropriate relationship and favoritism with a colleague rather than his handling of the Elizondo matter.
Correspondence between Luis Elizondo and DoD spokesperson Susan Gough was released by the Office of the Secretary of Defense under FOIA case 21-F-0938.
Bradley Hansell was confirmed by the Senate 61-35 as Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security and took office on 25 July 2025, succeeding acting Under Secretary Dustin Gard-Weiss.

dossier.denialPosture: OUSD(I&S) is the origin point of the central official denial in the modern UAP record: that Luis Elizondo had no responsibilities — later narrowed to 'no assigned responsibilities' — with regard to AATIP. That denial was formed internally in December 2017, withheld from the public for eighteen months, and issued through a departmental spokesperson rather than a signed official. It is contradicted in the same file by the department's own security officers, who feared Elizondo would release footage he had 'obtained during his employment with OUSD(I),' and by Reid's decision to open an AFOSI inquiry into his handling of that material.
dossier.narrative:
OUSD(I&S) is where the security state's plumbing and its press strategy meet, and the December 2017 file shows both running at once.

The charter first. DoD Directive 5143.01, reissued 24 October 2014 and updated by Change 2 on 6 April 2020, sets the USD(I&S)'s responsibilities, functions, relationships and authorities pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 113 and 137, 50 U.S.C. 3001 et seq., Public Law 108-458, and Executive Orders 12333, 13470 and 13869. The 'and Security' in the title was added in 2019-2020 and is the whole point: this office does not merely produce intelligence, it writes the rules for who may know things. It coordinates with the Director of the DoD Special Access Program Central Office on SAP matters involving ODNI and the intelligence community, and it runs the department's counterintelligence, law enforcement and security enterprise. Under 50 U.S.C. 3373(b)(3)(B)(i), enacted by Section 6802 of the FY2023 NDAA, the Director of AARO 'shall report... to the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security on all administrative matters of the Office.' Operational and security matters go to the Deputy Secretary and the Principal Deputy DNI; administration — staffing, funding, personnel, facilities — goes to OUSD(I&S). Congress placed the investigative body's housekeeping under the office whose predecessor had spent five years managing the Elizondo problem.

Now the file. Records obtained by The Black Vault under FOIA establish the sequence.

3 October 2017: Elizondo submits a resignation letter, received by his direct supervisor John Garrity III. A second, differently worded resignation letter — the one public since 2018 — is later characterized in Reid's memo as having 'uncertain provenance' and as never delivered to the Secretary of Defense.

12 October 2017: Reid learns of the To The Stars Academy launch, at which Elizondo appears as Director of Global Security and Special Programs one week after leaving DoD and states that TTSA plans to provide 'never-before-released footage from real U.S. government systems.' Reid contacts the Air Force Office of Special Investigations. AFOSI finds no 'tangible indicators' of misconduct and declines to open a case.

7 December 2017: The New York Times contacts DoD about AATIP and Elizondo.

15 December 2017: The OUSD(I) Security Officer is notified that Elizondo may have 'misused government systems' and 'may intend to release [U.S. government] footage or information that he obtained during his employment with OUSD(I).'

16 December 2017: 'Glowing Auras and Black Money' publishes, carrying the FLIR1 and Gimbal videos captioned as released by AATIP and courtesy of the Department of Defense. The same two videos appear on TTSA's YouTube channel.

18 December 2017: OUSD(I) discovers a classified email Elizondo sent to a Navy civilian in August 2017 requesting assistance getting videos declassified, with the same videos attached.

21 December 2017: Reid meets AFOSI agents to initiate a formal inquiry into Elizondo's possible mishandling of classified materials. AFOSI concludes the investigation in April 2018. No charges are known to have followed.

23 December 2017: A copy of Reid's memorandum for record carries handwritten marginal notes and initials dated '12/23' believed to be those of Secretary of Defense James N. Mattis, including a question whether Elizondo's 'sudden departure' was a 'counter-intelligence alarm?'

The two propositions in that file cannot both be casually true. If Elizondo had no job responsibilities related to AATIP, the department's own security office had no reason to fear that he would release government footage 'obtained during his employment with OUSD(I),' and Reid had no reason to open a counterintelligence inquiry about material he possessed. The counter-narrative and the counterintelligence action are internally inconsistent, and both were produced by the same office in the same week.

The eighteen-month gap is the other artifact. The determination was reached in December 2017. It was not made public until June 2019, when spokesman Christopher Sherwood told The Intercept that Elizondo 'had no responsibilities with regard to the AATIP program while he worked in OUSDI... up until the time he resigned effective 10/4/2017.' That formulation was later revised to 'no assigned responsibilities' — a lawyer's edit, narrowing a claim about what a man did to a claim about what was written in his position description. Departments do not narrow their own denials unless the broader version is indefensible.

Reid himself was removed in April 2022, following a nearly two-year investigation by The Debrief; the stated cause was an inappropriate relationship and favoritism with a colleague, not the Elizondo matter, and sources described him as the person most directly responsible for preventing further UAP video releases and for retaliating against Elizondo. The office continued. Bradley Hansell was confirmed as USD(I&S) by the Senate 61-35 and took office 25 July 2025, succeeding acting Under Secretary Dustin Gard-Weiss.

For an analyst the significance is structural rather than personal. The record shows that when a UAP disclosure event occurred, the response was generated inside OUSD(I&S) by the Director for Defense Intelligence, coordinated with a service investigative agency, briefed to the Secretary of Defense within a week, and held in reserve for eighteen months before public deployment. That is not confusion. That is an information operation run through a security-policy office — and the same office now holds administrative authority over AARO and coordination authority over DoD SAPs.
openQuestions: The exact date, control number and classification caveats of the Reid memorandum for record have not been established from the released copy; reporting places its classification at TS/ORCON but this was not verified against the document.
Why the December 2017 determination about Elizondo's role was withheld from the public for eighteen months before being issued through a spokesperson in June 2019.
Who authorized the change in wording from 'no responsibilities' to 'no assigned responsibilities,' and when.
What the New York Times submitted to DoD on 7 December 2017 that caused the OUSD(I) Security Officer to be notified on 15 December that Elizondo may have misused government systems.

Whether OUSD(I&S) or its predecessor exercised any authority over AATIP, AAWSAP or any successor effort beyond personnel administration, and whether any such authority is documented in a DoD issuance.
The identity of the 'Navy civilian' to whom Elizondo's August 2017 classified declassification-assistance email was addressed.
Whether the colleague who succeeded Reid after his April 2022 removal retained his UAP-related portfolio.

What administrative controls OUSD(I&S) has exercised over AARO's staffing, funding and access under 50 U.S.C. 3373(b)(3)(B)(i), and whether any of those controls have constrained AARO's historical record work.
dossier.whatItIs: The Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security, the OSD principal staff element for defense intelligence, counterintelligence, and security policy, chartered by DoD Directive 5143.01 (24 October 2014, incorporating Change 2, 6 April 2020) under 10 U.S.C. 113 and 137 and Executive Orders 12333, 13470 and 13869. It owns DoD security policy, counterintelligence, and the department's interface with the DoD Special Access Program Central Office. Under 50 U.S.C. 3373(b)(3)(B)(i), the Director of AARO reports to the USD(I&S) on all administrative matters of the office.
dossier.whyImplicated: OUSD(I&S) is the office that produced the paper trail of the Elizondo counter-narrative, and that paper trail is the cleanest documentary evidence in the entire record of a deliberate, dated, signed effort by a defense component to control the public account of a UAP program. Its Director for Defense Intelligence, Garry Reid, wrote a memorandum for record in late December 2017 — within a week of the New York Times AATIP story — asserting that Luis Elizondo had 'aggrandized his role' and that to the best of Reid's knowledge Elizondo 'had no job responsibilities related to the AATIP,' while simultaneously initiating an AFOSI inquiry into Elizondo's handling of classified material. The Pentagon then sat on that determination for eighteen months before deploying it publicly through spokesman Christopher Sherwood in June 2019, and afterwards quietly amended the wording from 'no responsibilities' to 'no assigned responsibilities.' The same office holds administrative authority over AARO, the body Congress created to investigate the concealment, and it is the department's SAP security-policy owner. The entity that ran the counter-narrative also holds the keys to the compartments and supervises the investigators.
